chapter.li: Verse5 Then he comes to the city of Samaria which is called Sychar, near to the parcel of ground which Jacob gave to his son Joseph, VerseEnd Verse6 the place where Jacob’s well was. Now Jesus, being weary with his journey, it being about the sixth hour, sat down on the well. VerseEnd Verse7 And there came a woman of Samaria to draw water. Jesus said unto her, Give me to drink. VerseEnd

Verse8 Now his disciples had gone away into the city to buy food; VerseEnd Verse9 wherefore, he being alone, the woman of Samaria said unto him, How is it that you, being a Jew, ask drink of me, who am a woman of Samaria? The Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans. VerseEnd

Verse10 Jesus answered and said unto her, If you knew the gift of God, and who it is who says to you, Give me to drink, you would have asked of him and he would have given you living water. VerseEnd Verse11 The woman said unto him, Sir, you have nothing to draw with and the well is deep. From where then do you have that living water? VerseEnd Verse12 Are you greater than our father Jacob, who gave us the well and drank thereof himself, and his children, and his cattle? VerseEnd Verse13 Jesus answered and said unto her, Whoever shall drink of this well shall thirst again, VerseEnd Verse14 but whoever drinks of the water which I shall give him shall never thirst, but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life. VerseEnd

Verse15 The woman said unto him, Sir, give me of this water, that I thirst not, neither come here to draw. VerseEnd Verse16 Jesus said unto her, Go, call your husband and come here. VerseEnd Verse17 The woman answered and said, I have no husband. Jesus said unto her, You have well said, I have no husband, VerseEnd Verse18 for you have had five husbands, and he whom you now have is not your husband. In that, said you truly. VerseEnd

Verse19 The woman said unto him, Sir, I perceive that you are a prophet. VerseEnd Verse20 Our fathers worshipped in this mountain, and you say that in Jerusalem is the place where men ought to worship. VerseEnd

Verse21 Jesus said unto her, Woman, believe me, the hour comes when you shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father. VerseEnd Verse22 You worship you know not what. We know what we worship, and salvation is of the Jews. VerseEnd Verse23 And the hour comes, and now is, when the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth. For the Father seeks such to worship him, VerseEnd Verse24 for unto such has God promised his spirit. And they who worship him must worship in spirit and in truth. VerseEnd

Verse25 The woman said unto him, I know that Messiah comes, who is called Christ. When he has come, he will tell us all things. VerseEnd Verse26 Jesus said unto her, I who speak unto you am the Messiah. VerseEnd

Verse27 And upon this came his disciples and marveled that he talked with the woman. Yet no man said, What do you seek? Or, why do you talk with her? VerseEnd Verse28 The woman then left her waterpot and went her way into the city, and says to the men, VerseEnd Verse29 Come see a man who told me all things that I have ever done. Is not this the Christ? VerseEnd Verse30 Then they went out of the city and came unto him. VerseEnd

Verse31 In the meantime, his disciples urged him, saying, Master, eat. VerseEnd Verse32 But he said unto them, I have food to eat that you know not of. VerseEnd Verse33 Therefore said the disciples one to another, Has any man brought him food to eat? VerseEnd Verse34 Jesus said unto them, My food is to do the will of him who sent me and to finish his work. VerseEnd Verse35 Do you not say, There are yet four months, then comes harvest? Behold, I say unto you, Lift up your eyes and look on the fields, for they are white already to harvest. VerseEnd Verse36 And he who reaps receives wages and gathers fruit unto life eternal, that both he who sows and he who reaps may rejoice together. VerseEnd Verse37 And herein is that saying true: One sows and another reaps. VerseEnd Verse38 I have sent you to reap that upon which you have expended no labor. The prophets have labored, and you have entered into their labors. VerseEnd

Verse39 And many of the Samaritans of that city believed on him for the saying of the woman who testified, saying, He told me all that I have ever done. VerseEnd Verse40 So when the Samaritans had come unto him, they implored him that he would stay with them. And he abided there two days. VerseEnd Verse41 And many more believed because of his own word VerseEnd Verse42 and said unto the woman, Now we believe, not because of your saying. We have heard for ourselves and know that this is indeed the Christ, the Savior of the world. VerseEnd

Verse43 Now after two days, he departed from there and went into Galilee, VerseEnd Verse44 for Jesus himself testified that a prophet has no honor in his own country. VerseEnd Verse45 Then when he had come into Galilee, the Galileans received him, having seen all the things which he had done at Jerusalem at the feast, for they also went unto the feast. VerseEnd

Verse46 So Jesus came again into Cana of Galilee where he made the water wine. And there was a certain nobleman whose son was sick at Capernaum. VerseEnd Verse47 When he heard Jesus had come out of Judea into Galilee, he went unto him and implored him that he would come down and heal his son, for he was at the point of death. VerseEnd Verse48 Then said Jesus unto him, Except you see signs and wonders, you will not believe. VerseEnd Verse49 The nobleman said unto him, Sir, come down before my child die. VerseEnd Verse50 Jesus said unto him, Go your way, your son lives. And the man believed the word which Jesus had spoken unto him and he went his way. VerseEnd Verse51 And as he was now going down to his house, his servants met him and spoke, saying, Your son lives. VerseEnd Verse52 Then inquired he of them the hour when he began to amend. And they said unto him, Yesterday at the seventh hour, the fever left him. VerseEnd Verse53 So the father knew that his son was healed in the same hour in which Jesus said unto him, Your son lives. And he believed, and his whole house, VerseEnd Verse54 this being the second miracle which Jesus had done when he had come out of Judea into Galilee. VerseEnd
LEChapter5 Verse1 After this, there was a feast of the Jews. And Jesus went up to Jerusalem. VerseEnd
